L01 | Judgment remains in deciding when the evidence is strong enough to name a cause and when a paraphrase has shifted the meaning of someone else's words.
L02 | Judgment remains in deciding how to mark a time as estimated when no clock reading is available and which records need exact times.
L03 | Judgment remains in choosing which lessons deserve to become fixed steps, where those steps belong in the workflow, and when a step has outlived its purpose.
L04 | Judgment remains in deciding how much evidence a particular claim needs and how strongly to word a claim that rests on thin support.
L05 | Judgment remains in deciding which repeated facts carry enough weight to test, what counts as an adequate test, and which nearby caveats must travel with the fact.
L06 | Judgment remains in recognizing which strings are exact identifiers that must be machine-copied and when a shortened form is acceptable if clearly labeled.
L07 | Judgment remains in deciding which other sources could plausibly change the answer and when the search has gone far enough to stop.
L08 | Judgment remains in deciding whether an empty or short result comes from a sound search or a broken one and how much further to look before reporting.
L09 | Judgment remains in choosing what evidence of the actual outcome is enough, such as a full count, a sample, or a spot check, for the stakes involved.
L10 | Judgment remains in weighing how much more checking is warranted against the urgency of the situation before declaring something lost or taking an irreversible recovery step.
L11 | Judgment remains in reading what kind of attention the person is asking for and recognizing when, if ever, it becomes appropriate to offer more.
L12 | Judgment remains in deciding what observable behavior counts as proof that a change is in effect and how long to watch for it.
L13 | Judgment remains in identifying which single check actually decides whether the claim of done or verified is true.
L14 | Judgment remains in deciding which neighboring parts count as beside the fix and how widely to check before calling the fix complete.
L15 | Judgment remains in deciding which outside sources are reliable enough to count as a check and whether a partial check justifies anything stronger than not checked.
L16 | Judgment remains in deciding which work is important enough for a second reviewer and which reviewer is different enough to catch what the first would miss.
L17 | Judgment remains in choosing a forced failure that is realistic and safe to induce and deciding which tests and monitors need this treatment and how often.
